ADR 0009 amends 0001: source state (ticket files, plans) is worktree-local and tracked, so a change rides the branch that made it and merges per file; derived state (index, rollup, leases, telemetry) resolves through the git common dir and is never tracked. ADR 0001 chose common-dir resolution to prevent a split-brain append-only log, a reason that per-ticket files remove. ADR 0010 records the ticket record shape (ticket, ordered events, external mapping), the invariants (one file per ticket, owner by scope.repo, a prefix is not an owner, edges carry a locator, a duplicate uuid is corruption) and the integration seam: an external field plus a written adapter contract, explicitly not an implementation.

DONE 2026-11-08 (commit cdf4bd3, docs/decisions/0010-a-ticket-is-a-file.md).

The ticket-record contract is written down now that the migration has run and other code depends on it: one file
per ticket, identity is the task uuid, a duplicate uuid is corruption rather than a merge, the owner is scope.repo,
a key prefix is a minting convention and never an owner, edges reference with a locator instead of copying, replay
orders by the record, and writes are exclusive and atomic.

Also recorded: the integration seam (an external field, no adapter, and why building one before knowing the
workflow is how a six-step epic closes at 0/6), and an explicit "what this does not decide" section - rendering the
locator, and the judgement still required when a crate name is ambiguous.

ADR 0009 decided which copy of state a command sees; 0010 decides what a ticket is. ADR 0001's ledger append is
superseded by both while its rule about where state lives stands.
